title: ChatGPT is poorly designed. So I fixed it

primary.label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors

summary: Ben Holmes argues that ChatGPT, despite massive adoption, has fundamental design flaws stemming from disconnected feature teams—a phenomenon Scott Hanselman calls "shipping the org chart." The core problem is demonstrated through a voice conversation where ChatGPT can compose a written email but can only respond via voice, forcing users to end the call and search transcripts for formatted text. Voice and text modes feel like products from different companies, and model selection is cluttered with confusing names resembling a science fair of options. Holmes proposes two fixes. First, enable simultaneous voice and text interaction so users can speak while receiving and editing written responses in real time. Second, implement smart model routing that automatically selects the appropriate model based on request complexity. Both are achievable with existing tools: GPT-4o Realtime for live audio, tool calls for text-based communication, and reasoning models for complex queries. The proposed app design features a voice mode with a floating orb interface plus a new chat button that opens an iMessage-like panel, allowing users to see formatted text responses—like email drafts or links—while continuing the voice conversation. Holmes demonstrates this routing pattern through Warp terminal, which handles simple requests like "undo my last commit" directly but routes complex tasks like "refactor this entire codebase to use Flutter" to a reasoning model that first writes a plan. The technical implementation relies on tool calls rather than elaborate system prompts. A "send chat message" tool handles text delivery for content easier to read than hear, while a separate tool sends off to reasoning models for deeper queries. Holmes notes the model intelligently determines when to use each tool based on description alone, underscoring how far simple prompting has advanced. The complete source code is available on GitHub under fixgpt.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: ChatGPT's Growth and Confusing Design
sections.summary: Introduction highlighting that ChatGPT is one of the fastest-growing apps in history with hundreds of millions of daily users, yet no one has stopped to ask why the app is so confusing.

sections.title: Voice Mode Limitations Demonstrated
sections.summary: Demo showing ChatGPT's two voice options (voice-to-text and voice-to-voice). A request to write a group email about the AI Engineer World's Fair succeeds, but the response can only come back through voice, not as collaborative text.

sections.title: Shipping the Org Chart
sections.summary: Scott Hanselman's concept of 'shipping the org chart' explained via an EV analogy where the map, climate, and speedometer use different fonts—revealing the company's organizational structure. OpenAI is guilty too, shipping disconnected features with confusing model names.

sections.title: Proposed Fixes: Multimodal and Multi-Model
sections.summary: Two changes proposed: allowing voice and text simultaneously, and smartly choosing the right model based on the ask. Achievable with off-the-shelf tools like GPT-4o Realtime for live audio and tool calls for text and reasoning handoffs.

sections.title: App Design Concept
sections.summary: The fixgpt app design features a voice mode with a floating orb, mute, end call, and a new chat button that opens an iMessage-like panel for text responses during voice calls, enabling simultaneous voice and text collaboration.

sections.title: Warp Terminal Demo
sections.summary: Warp terminal demonstrates the routing pattern: simple requests like 'undo my last commit' are handled directly by a coding agent, while complex requests like refactoring to Flutter trigger a reasoning model that writes a plan first.

sections.title: Implementation with Tool Calls
sections.summary: Live demo using a 'send chat message' tool for text details and a reasoning handoff tool for deeper queries. The model intelligently uses tools based on description alone without a system prompt. Source code available on GitHub at fixgpt.
